column1: # (internal/core/check_then_act_lock_guard_test.go). Every hit from this guard's first run
# (31) was read against the real code and classified below. The first classification said
# none was a genuine cross-replica race; the independent second review (see the review
# column and the block below) found 13 that are. See
# Independent second review (C-GUARD2-EXEMPT-REVIEW, #2564, 2026-10-03): every row was
# re-read against the code on main (callees down to the SQL issued) and its "safe" claim
# tested against a concrete two-replica Postgres interleaving. The review column records
# the verdict: CONFIRMED (class and reason accurate), RECLASSIFIED (conclusion holds, class
# and/or reason rewritten), or UNSAFE (a real cross-replica check-then-act gap: class set to
# UNSAFE-OPEN, reason names the tracking issue and the skipped Postgres race test in
# it). UNSAFE-OPEN rows stay in this file — removing them would turn the guard red without
# fixing anything — until the fixing PR un-skips its test and drops/relabels the row.
#   SERIAL-EQUIV  the check reads state another actor can change concurrently, but every
#                 interleaving's end state equals some serial order of the two operations.
#   STALE         no longer a guard hit on main (checked by removing the row: the guard
#                 stays green); kept because review does not delete rows. NOTE: the guard
#                 does not detect stale rows, so these do not fail anything.
#   UNSAFE-OPEN   a confirmed open race; see the issue in the reason.
#   PARENT-LOCKED was UNSAFE-OPEN: a child row (share, ACL grant, lease, environment, config)
#                 could commit under a concurrently deleted parent. Now closed in storage:
#                 the child write and a FOR SHARE re-read of the live parent run in one
#                 transaction, which rolls back if the parent is gone (lockLiveParent,
#                 INV-STORE-21). The guard sees only WithNamedLock, not a row lock, so the
#                 row stays, with the reason naming the conditional write and its test.

column3: #2655: requireReauth itself is safe, but ActivateMFASecret (local_mfa.go:31, UPDATE ... WHERE user_id=?) does not pin the TOTP secret validated at mfa.go:96-100; a concurrent BeginMFAEnrollment swap gets activated. Demonstrated: TestCTAReview_ActivateMFA_vs_BeginMFAEnrollment_CrossReplicaPostgres.

requireSecret (secret_dependencies.go) only checks existence; edges outlive soft-delete by design, so a racing DeleteSecret equals serial add-then-delete; the peer is authorized separately. The integrity-relevant check (the cycle check) is not this require* call but CreateSecretDependencyExclusive's own read, and since #2660 that read-check-insert runs under WithNamedLock(secretDependencyGraphLockKey(project)) inside LockedCreateSecretDependencyExclusive, which every edge-adding caller goes through, so two replicas can no longer both commit A->B and B->A (TestCTAReview_AddSecretDependency_CrossReplicaCycle_Postgres). The guard still flags this row because requireSecret precedes the locked helper.
column4: reviewed_by=C-GUARD2-EXEMPT-REVIEW; verdict=RECLASSIFIED (reason corrected: "atomic DB primitive" claim was false)

column3: storage.UpdateAccessRequest is a conditional UPDATE ... WHERE state='pending' (returns ok bool), fails closed on a stale read; requireAdminAuthorityAt is an actor-authority check unrelated to the race; see #2564.

#2651: the insert commits on its own (the row IS visible — the in-code comment at dynamic_secrets.go:240 is wrong); the second full-row Save (:263) writes disabled=false over a concurrent DeleteProject disable (#369). Demonstrated: TestCTAReview_CreateDynamicSecretConfig_vs_DeleteProject_CrossReplicaPostgres.
requireAdminAuthorityAt is an actor-authority check, not shared mutable state; see #2564.

The ceiling checks (users.go:336-416) and SoD set-check (:363) target a principal that does not exist until CreateUserWithRoleGrants (:365) commits it and its grants atomically, so no concurrent grant can address it; the flagged AddPasswordHistory (:378) is a best-effort history row. Residual: a concurrently created SoD policy can miss the new user — common to every grant path; see #2564.
column4: reviewed_by=C-GUARD2-EXEMPT-REVIEW; verdict=RECLASSIFIED (was AUTHZ-ACTOR; reason omitted the real write)

column3: requireUserCredentialsRevokeAuthority is an actor-authority check; the revoke write is idempotent and lock-free-safe per inventory item 16; see #2564.

column3: requireReauth (webauthn.go:160) re-verifies credentials; its single-use inputs (TOTP step, step-up grant) and the ceremony itself (ConsumeWebAuthnSession, local_webauthn.go: WHERE used_at IS NULL) are conditional updates, and credential_id is unique-indexed, so stale reads are serial-equivalent; see #2564.

#2649: requireSecretOrFolderNode is the liveness fact DeleteSecret's CWE-284 ACL cascade (local_secrets.go:600) depends on; a racing DeleteSecret lets the upsert (secret_acl.go:108) land an ACL on the deleted secret, reactivating on restore. Demonstrated: TestCTAReview_GrantSecretACL_vs_DeleteSecret_CrossReplicaPostgres.

No longer a guard hit on main: the require* checks moved into buildGlobalInvite (invitations.go:392-422), which writes nothing. Would be safe anyway: the write is a pending invitation granting nothing, and accept re-runs ceiling + SoD under sodGrantLockKey (invitations.go:497-515). Row kept per #2564 (rows are never deleted by review).

No longer a guard hit on main: the require* check moved into buildProjectInvite (invitations.go:139), which writes nothing. Would be safe anyway: the write is a pending invitation granting nothing, and accept re-runs ceiling + SoD under sodGrantLockKey (invitations.go:497-515). Row kept per #2564.

#2652: requireLiveProjectAndEnvironment is the #369 gate, not a bare existence check; a DeleteProject committing between it (dynamic_secrets.go:493) and CreateDynamicSecretLease (:570) lists leases before this one exists, leaving an active, never-revoked credential. Demonstrated: TestCTAReview_IssueLease_vs_DeleteProject_CrossReplicaPostgres.

requireSecret is an existence/accessibility check, not the race-relevant decision; see #2564.

Both guards and the write run inside withGroupProjectAdminGuardLocks (project_members.go:439), which holds lastAdminGuardLockKey PLUS every affected projectAdminGuardLockKey(P), sorted (#2352). Documented residual: the project set is computed before the per-project locks (project_members.go:431). Related non-race last-admin gap on the direct-removal path: #2658.

column3: A stale liveness pass cannot revive a credential: the cascade's RevokeLease drops it on the target, so the end credential state is serial-equivalent. Side note (LOW, bookkeeping): UpdateDynamicSecretLease is a stale full-row Save (local_dynamic.go:108) that can flip a concurrently revoked lease row back to active while the credential stays dead; see #2564.

#2656: the core ceiling check is serial-equivalent (it reads the project grant set, not only the actor), but LocalStorage.RestoreEnvironment checks project liveness in one autocommit SELECT (local_secrets.go:670) and un-deletes in a separate UPDATE (:426); a DeleteProject between them leaves a live environment under a deleted project. Demonstrated: TestCTAReview_RestoreEnvironment_vs_DeleteProject_CrossReplicaPostgres.

No longer a guard hit on main: GetGroupRoles, requireGlobalAdminToReinstateAdminRoles and tx.RestoreGroup all run inside WithNamedLock(sodGrantLockKey("group", id)) (groups.go:177-198, #2469). The original reason ("not shared mutable state") was wrong: the check reads the group's role set. Row kept per #2564.

column3: requireAdminRankCeilingForTarget reads target AND actor roles (not actor-only); a stale pass equals revoke-then-promote and only removes access; the write is an idempotent DELETE (local_auth.go:213). Inventory item 16 (revocation honored on next read) is a different property; see #2564.

#2650: the admin gate depends on a stale read of RotationBackend (rotation_executor.go:744) and the write is UpdateSecret's full-row Save of that snapshot (:759) — it undeletes a concurrently deleted secret (GORM Save upsert fallback), strips a concurrent admin binding (#90), and restores cleared ownership. Demonstrated: TestCTAReview_SetSecretAutoRotate_vs_DeleteSecret_CrossReplicaPostgres.

#2646: the ownership side is serial-equivalent, but the secret's liveness is not — a DeleteSecret committing between CreateShareRecord's reads and its INSERT (local_sharing.go:76) leaves a live share on a deleted secret (#370 bypass). Demonstrated: TestCTAReview_ShareSecret_vs_DeleteSecret_CrossReplicaPostgres.

#2647: same CreateShareRecord window as ShareSecret (#2646) — a racing DeleteSecret leaves a live group share on the deleted secret. The check also reads recipient-group scope, not only the actor. Demonstrated: TestCTAReview_ShareSecretWithGroup_vs_DeleteSecret_CrossReplicaPostgres.

requireEqualOrGreaterAdminAuthority reads target AND actor roles (not actor-only); a stale pass equals start-then-role-change, and ReauthorizeImpersonation re-checks the ceiling on every session validation (auth.go, 60s cache in authz.go), bounding the session exactly as in the serial case; see #2564.

#2657: the flagged ceiling->RemoveProjectMember pair is locked (projectAdminGuardLockKey), but nothing locks the state CAS (membership_lifecycle.go:336) together with the grant (:347): a revoke landing between activation's CAS and its grant reports success and ends `revoked` with a live grant. Demonstrated: TestCTAReview_TransitionMembership_ActivateVsRevoke_CrossReplicaPostgres.

#2654: not nested-locked — UpdateOwnProfile never sets IsActive, so UpdateUser takes its unlocked default branch; the full-row write (Select("*"), gated only on is_active) reverts a concurrent password change / suspension / MFA enable, with only a session. Demonstrated: TestCTAReview_UpdateOwnProfile_vs_ChangePassword_CrossReplicaPostgres.

#2648: UpdateShareRecord persists with GORM Save(struct); against a concurrently revoked (soft-deleted) share the UPDATE matches 0 rows and GORM falls back to INSERT ... ON CONFLICT DO UPDATE SET <all columns> incl. deleted_at=NULL, resurrecting the share. Demonstrated: TestCTAReview_UpdateSharePermission_vs_RevokeShare_CrossReplicaPostgres.

#2653: not a control-flow FP — the ceiling check (users.go:499) precedes every branch. Every branch writes the full pre-read row (UpdateUserIfActiveStateMatches, Select("*"), gated only on is_active), reverting concurrent SetAccountState (suspension), SetPasswordHash, MFA and lockout writes. Last-admin itself is correctly locked. Demonstrated: TestCTAReview_UpdateUser_vs_SuspendUser_CrossReplicaPostgres.

Both guards and the write run inside withGroupProjectAdminGuardLocks (project_members.go:439): lastAdminGuardLockKey PLUS every affected projectAdminGuardLockKey(P), sorted (#2352). Documented residual: the project set is computed before the per-project locks (project_members.go:431). Related non-race last-admin gap: #2658.

column3: #2659: AddProjectMember takes no lock — the lock that applies is AssignUserRole's sodGrantLockKey("user") (inventory item 3, not item 10), covering only SoD+AssignRole; in open mode the membership commits `active` (membership_lifecycle.go:211) before the grant (:225), so a revoke between ends `revoked` with a live grant.
